item.title: The Ultimate Single GitHub Actions CI/CD File: Go, Node, Flutter, Dart, Qt/C++, Docker, and Packaging
item.author: technicalblog123@arran4.com (Arran Ubels)
item.description: This is a practical build-up guide for creating one large ci.yml that is still readable, maintainable, and tailored to real repositories. The target outcome: One workflow file handles push, PR open/update, PR close, tags, release publish, manual dispatch, and monthly/nightly schedules. It supports mixed repos: Go, Node, Dart, Flutter, Qt/C++, classic C/Makefile, and Dockerized components. It can run in public mode (broader checks) or private mode (cost-controlled), while keeping default test runners Ubuntu unless cross-OS coverage is explicitly needed.

item.title: From Patch to Playbook: A Repeatable Process for Refactoring CLI Help Text
item.author: technicalblog123@arran4.com (Arran Ubels)
item.description: A recent patch series for arran4/git-tag-inc (PR #54) is a good example of how to turn a one-off code change into a repeatable method other projects can use. The technical change was simple: move long CLI help text out of Go code and into an embedded template, keep dynamic values in code, shift conditional rendering into the template, and avoid global flag-output side effects. The process is what matters most, because it is reusable across repos and agent-assisted workflows.

item.title: GitHub Actions + golangci-lint: Go Version Compatibility Matrix (with Copy/Paste Workflows)
item.author: technicalblog123@arran4.com (Arran Ubels)
item.description: If you use this in GitHub Actions: 1 2 3 4 - name: golangci-lint uses: golangci/golangci-lint-action@v9 with: version: latest you are absolutely right to be cautious: latest can move to a new golangci-lint release that adds support for a new Go minor while your workflow, runner, or repo expectations are still pinned to older assumptions. This guide gives you: a practical version pairing table (Go ↔ golangci-lint ↔ action), safe version ranges you can reuse, and many copy/paste workflow examples.

item.title: Git Refs and Refspecs: Grammar Reference
item.author: technicalblog123@arran4.com (Arran Ubels)
item.description: Git’s ref system is a tiny language for naming objects and mapping them across repositories. This post is a grammar reference first, and examples second.
